variants.title: Celebrity post spike
variants.context: A viral post is read 150,000 times in two minutes, but the database is still serving the same row over and over.
variants.constraint: The content is identical across reads and does not change often.
variants.question: What is your primary optimization?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a cache-aside layer with a TTL and invalidation on update.
wrongChoices: Move all reads to the primary

variants.title: Checkout page hot object
variants.context: A single product is hit by 80% of traffic during a flash sale.
variants.constraint: The page content rarely changes and is highly repetitive.
variants.question: Where should the repeated reads be served from?
variants.expectedPattern: A cache in front of the product read path.

variants.title: Profile storm
variants.context: A popular profile hits the same data repeatedly during a launch campaign.
variants.constraint: Reads dominate; writes are minimal.
variants.question: What pattern offsets the repeated database work?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache profile data and invalidate when updates are made.
wrongChoices: Add a reader-only database without caching
Move profile state into local memory

variants.title: Inventory freshness
variants.context: Inventory values change every few minutes and are read constantly across the app.
variants.constraint: The system can tolerate a small delay but not stale inventory for long.
variants.question: What is the best tradeoff?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a short TTL with invalidation on stock updates.

variants.title: Cache stampede
variants.context: A hot object expires and 8,000 requests miss at once.
variants.constraint: The DB sees a synchronized cold miss from many clients.
variants.question: What prevents the stampede?
variants.expectedPattern: Single-flight refresh or lock around the first miss.

variants.title: Regional traffic burst
variants.context: A local event sends heavy reads to a regional page from one city.
variants.constraint: Most requests hit the same few objects and the origin is far away.
variants.question: Where should the data live for fastest response?
variants.expectedPattern: A regional cache close to users and a shorter TTL on the hot object.

variants.title: Leaderboard freshness
variants.context: A leaderboard updates every 20 seconds but is read continuously.
variants.constraint: A few seconds of staleness is acceptable.
variants.question: What is the right cache policy?
variants.expectedPattern: Short TTL with periodic refresh and invalidation on score changes.

variants.title: Hot user object
variants.context: One user profile object is fetched millions of times per hour, yet the underlying record changes occasionally.
variants.constraint: The data is user-specific and easy to invalidate.
variants.question: How do you keep reads cheap without stale sessions?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache the user metadata with a short expiry and invalidate on update/logout.
wrongChoices: Store it in a single process memory

variants.title: Flash-sale pricing page
variants.context: The same pricing page is hit by thousands of users when a price update happens.
variants.constraint: The pricing data updates infrequently but is read frequently.
variants.question: What is the best design decision?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache product display data and invalidate on pricing updates.

variants.title: Sparse but repeated reads
variants.context: A document or special report is rare but requested heavily for a few minutes.
variants.constraint: A cold object causes a big latency spike and repeated DB hits.
variants.question: How should the system handle the first miss?
variants.expectedPattern: Populate the cache once and serve the rest from memory.
wrongChoices: Use CDN only for dynamic content

variants.title: Config flags hit the database
variants.context: Every request loads feature flags from SQL, adding 15ms even though flags change hourly.
variants.constraint: Flags are tiny, shared, and rarely written.
variants.question: Where should flags live at request time?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache flags in memory or Redis with invalidation when an admin publishes a change.
wrongChoices: Join flags into every user query
Store flags only in client localStorage
Recompute flags from logs on each request

variants.title: Negative caching missing
variants.context: Bots request missing product IDs and each 404 still queries the primary.
variants.constraint: Most of those IDs will never exist.
variants.question: What cache behavior stops the waste?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache negative lookups (short TTL) so repeated misses do not hit the database.
wrongChoices: Return 200 with empty HTML from the origin every time

variants.title: Write-through vs stampede on prices
variants.context: Price updates land in SQL, but readers still miss cache for 30s after each change.
variants.constraint: Readers must see new prices quickly without a thundering herd.
variants.question: What write path keeps the cache coherent?
variants.expectedPattern: Invalidate or write-through the cache on price update so the next read is cheap and fresh.
wrongChoices: Flush the entire cache on one price change
Write prices only to cache and never to SQL

variants.title: Session cache as source of truth
variants.context: A Redis cache is treated as durable session storage and a node restart logs everyone out.
variants.constraint: Sessions must survive cache eviction.
variants.question: What is the correct cache role?
variants.expectedPattern: Use cache as a fast layer in front of durable session storage, not as the only copy.
wrongChoices: Increase Redis maxmemory and skip persistence
Store sessions only in browser cookies without a server record
Disable eviction and hope memory never fills

variants.title: Multi-key assemble on every page
variants.context: A homepage fans out to 40 independent DB keys that almost never change together.
variants.constraint: The assembled page is identical for anonymous users for minutes.
variants.question: What should be cached?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache the assembled homepage fragment, not only the individual keys.
wrongChoices: Cache nothing because keys are small
Query all 40 keys on every request
Move the 40 keys into one giant unindexed table

variants.title: Hot key eviction loop
variants.context: A tiny Redis instance evicts the hottest key, which is immediately reloaded and evicted again.
variants.constraint: Working set is larger than cache RAM.
variants.question: What stops the thrash?
variants.expectedPattern: Size the cache for the hot working set or split hot keys so they are not constantly evicted.
wrongChoices: Set TTL to zero on everything
Disable eviction and OOM the cache

variants.title: Personalized feed over-cached
variants.context: User A sees User B’s feed because a shared cache key ignored user id.
variants.constraint: Feeds are private per user.
variants.question: What is the cache-key rule?
variants.expectedPattern: Include user identity (and auth scope) in the cache key for personalized data.
wrongChoices: One global feed key for everyone
Cache HTML without Vary on cookie

variants.title: Computed report on every dashboard open
variants.context: A 12-second aggregation runs on each dashboard load even when filters are unchanged.
variants.constraint: The report can be a few minutes stale.
variants.question: How do you cut dashboard latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache the computed result keyed by filters, with a TTL or refresh job.
wrongChoices: Run the aggregation in the browser
Lock the dashboard until the query finishes every time
Increase DB parallelism for identical queries

variants.title: Dogpile after deploy
variants.context: A deploy flushes Redis and the primary instantly takes the full read load.
variants.constraint: The working set is large and popular.
variants.question: How should deploys treat the cache?
variants.expectedPattern: Avoid full flush; warm or version keys so the origin is not stampeded.
wrongChoices: Turn the cache off during deploys

variants.title: Local in-process cache drifts
variants.context: Each app instance caches config in memory and instances disagree for 10 minutes after a change.
variants.constraint: All instances must converge quickly.
variants.question: What cache design fixes drift?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a shared cache or pub/sub invalidation so every instance drops the stale entry.
